_comment: The six theses that survived review. Twenty-two raw extractions from three research documents, consolidated by hand into six independent claims. The originals are archived under data/theses.raw/ - nothing was deleted. See CONSOLIDATION.md for why each merge or cut was made.

theses.claim: BWXT Commercial Operations revenue grows at least 45% for FY2026, in line with raised guidance.
theses.mechanism: Merchant supplier position across reactor designs plus recent acquisitions drive commercial revenue; Q2 2026 commercial revenue grew 72% including 33% organic.
kill_criteria: FY2026 Commercial Operations revenue growth comes in below 45%.
theses.source_document: FY2026 Form 10-K or Q4 2026 earnings release, segment revenue table
absorbed_from: nuclear renaissance capture regardless of design
strong commercial demand drives growth
may miss near-term growth targets on order timing
growth half of the bundled slower-growth bear thesis

theses.claim: BWXT Commercial Operations adjusted EBITDA margin for FY2026 lands at or above the lowered 13% guidance, and free cash flow comes in at or above the guided floor of $345M.
theses.mechanism: Management is spending ahead of orders - capex near 6% of sales rising toward 7% - and lowered commercial margin guidance from about 14% to about 13% to fund US capacity. The claim is that the lowered bar still holds.
kill_criteria: FY2026 Commercial Operations adjusted EBITDA margin comes in below 13%, or FY2026 free cash flow comes in below $345M.
theses.source_document: FY2026 Form 10-K or Q4 2026 earnings release
absorbed_from: capacity investment compresses margins and FCF
margin half of the bundled slower-growth bear thesis

theses.claim: BWXT Government Operations revenue grows at least 7% for FY2026, in line with high-single-digit guidance.
theses.mechanism: Naval propulsion demand plus DOE work. Note this requires meaningful acceleration: Q2 2026 government revenue grew only 2%, so the back half must carry the year.
kill_criteria: FY2026 Government Operations revenue growth comes in below 7%.
absorbed_from: government operations will show weak growth (reframed - original bet against guidance, now tests whether guidance is met)
government budget concentration vulnerability

theses.claim: The four-year Ford-class carrier procurement cadence holds and submarine procurement stays at two Virginia-class plus one Columbia-class per year through FY2028.
theses.mechanism: The four-year carrier cadence removes historical gap years, keeping two reactor sets in continuous production. Steady submarine rates keep the specialised workforce utilised.
kill_criteria: Any Navy 30-year shipbuilding plan or enacted appropriation through FY2028 reduces Ford-class cadence beyond four years, or cuts Virginia-class below two per year, or cuts Columbia-class below one per year.
theses.source_document: US Navy 30-year shipbuilding plan (annual) and enacted NDAA / defense appropriations
absorbed_from: predictable naval demand under updated shipbuilding plan
sole-source domestic naval manufacturer moat
four-year carrier cycle improves revenue stability

theses.claim: Sterling E-Infrastructure revenue grows at least 50% year over year in at least one of the next two quarters, and signed backlog stays above $4.0B.
theses.mechanism: Data centre and semiconductor construction demand; Q2 2026 E-Infrastructure revenue rose 192% to $905M with mission-critical work at 92% of segment backlog. Labour constraints, if binding, show up here as growth deceleration. Revenue in this business is lumpy by project timing, so a single soft quarter is tolerated deliberately - two consecutive soft quarters is the signal.
kill_criteria: E-Infrastructure revenue growth falls below 50% year over year in both of the next two quarters.
Signed backlog falls below $4.0B in any quarterly report through February 2027.
theses.source_document: Sterling quarterly earnings releases, segment revenue and backlog
absorbed_from: dominant in mission-critical digital infrastructure
record backlog provides revenue visibility
regional expansion into high-growth markets
electrician shortage caps growth (observable only as deceleration)

theses.claim: Sterling E-Infrastructure segment operating margin holds at or above the prior-year level for two consecutive quarters, despite lower-margin electrical work growing faster than site development.
theses.mechanism: Electrical work runs near 12% margins against high-20s for site development. Management targets 3-5 points of electrical margin improvement over 18 months. The claim is that mix shift does not outrun that improvement. Note the deliberate asymmetry with the revenue thesis: revenue is lumpy by project timing so one soft quarter is tolerated, but margin is a rate and a single year-over-year decline is exactly the dilution signal this thesis is watching for, so one quarter is enough to fire.
kill_criteria: E-Infrastructure segment operating margin falls year over year in either of the next two quarters.
theses.source_document: Sterling quarterly earnings releases, segment operating margin
absorbed_from: disciplined capital reallocation drives margin expansion (bull)
electrical mix dilutes consolidated margins (bear)
CEC integration creates a moat (observable only through margins)

theses.claim: BWXT Government Operations revenue grows at least 7% in FY2027 compared with FY2026, in line with high-single-digit guidance.
theses.mechanism: Special Materials ramp (high-purity depleted uranium, defense fuels) plus Naval Propulsion and Advanced Nuclear growth; management guided high single to low double digit.
kill_criteria: FY2027 Government Operations revenue is less than 1.07 times FY2026 Government Operations revenue.
absorbed_from: Motley Fool, BWXT Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-11-02), capture item #2, kill criterion rewritten by hand

theses.claim: BWXT Commercial Operations adjusted EBITDA margin improves by at least 0.5 percentage points in FY2027 compared with FY2026.
theses.mechanism: Higher volume, operational improvements and better absorption of growth investments; management guided +50 to 100 basis points.
kill_criteria: FY2027 Commercial Operations adjusted EBITDA margin minus FY2026, both as shown side by side in BWXT's Q4 2027 earnings release, is less than +0.5 percentage points.
theses.source_document: Q4 2027 earnings release (exhibit 99.1), segment adjusted EBITDA table
absorbed_from: Motley Fool, BWXT Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-11-02), capture item #4, kill criterion rewritten by hand

theses.claim: BWXT FY2027 free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures) is at least as high as FY2026.
theses.mechanism: Earnings growth lifts operating cash flow, partly offset by working capital, capital spending near 6% of revenue and a pension headwind; management guided flat to slightly higher.
kill_criteria: FY2027 operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, from the FY2027 Form 10-K cash flow statement, is lower than the same figure for FY2026.
absorbed_from: Motley Fool, BWXT Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-11-02), capture item #5, kill criterion rewritten by hand

theses.claim: BWXT announces, by February 28, 2027, that it made a final investment decision on or before December 31, 2026 to build a new U.S. plant for large steam generators and reactor pressure vessels.
theses.mechanism: Design details are being finalized and management said the decision does not depend on firm orders; target is year-end 2026.
kill_criteria: By February 28, 2027, BWXT has not stated in a press release, SEC filing or earnings call that it made this final investment decision on or before December 31, 2026.
theses.source_document: BWXT press releases, 8-K filings, Q4 2026 earnings release and call
absorbed_from: Motley Fool, BWXT Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-11-02), capture item #7, kill criterion rewritten by hand

theses.claim: BWXT announces, by June 30, 2027, its first firm order for major components (such as reactor pressure vessels or steam generators) for a new U.S. nuclear reactor build, including small modular reactors.
theses.mechanism: Active discussions with reactor vendors on U.S. builds; CEO expected new U.S. build orders by year-end 2026 and no later than about the first half of 2027.
kill_criteria: By June 30, 2027, BWXT has not announced a signed contract to supply major components (such as reactor pressure vessels or steam generators) for a new U.S. reactor build, including small modular reactors (selections, memoranda of understanding, letters of intent and refurbishment or life-extension orders do not count).
theses.source_document: BWXT press releases, 8-K filings, Q1 and Q2 2027 earnings releases and calls
absorbed_from: Motley Fool, BWXT Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-11-02), capture item #9, kill criterion rewritten by hand

cut.claim: Management will continue to unlock shareholder value through disciplined capital allocation
cut.reason: Not testable. An endorsement rather than a claim - no observation settles it.

cut.claim: The stock is priced too highly at about 36x forward earnings
cut.reason: Inherently price-based. Measures the market, not the business.

cut.claim: mPower licensing will generate high-margin royalty revenue
cut.reason: BWXT does not break out royalty or licensing income as a separate line. Permanently unobservable.

cut.claim: The medical divestiture will sharpen focus and fund expansion
cut.reason: Resolves within months and says nothing durable about the business.

cut.claim: Housing weakness will keep dragging on Building Solutions
cut.reason: 9% of revenue, already declining, not why anyone owns the stock. Not worth tracking.
